items.title: The Korean War killed around 3 million people
items.claim: What was the death toll of the Korean War (June 1950-July 1953)?

options.text: Estimates centre around 3 million dead, mostly Korean civilians; nearly 37,000 US, around 1,000 British and Commonwealth, and over 400,000 Chinese troops killed
Comparable to WWI losses for the Allies

items.reveal:
North Korea invaded south of the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950. UN forces under General MacArthur landed at Inchon (September 1950) and pushed to the Yalu River; China entered in October-November.

The armistice was signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953. There has never been a peace treaty — the two Koreas are still technically at war. Pyongyang was reduced by US bombing to perhaps 25% of its buildings; an estimated 20% of North Korea's population died.

In the US, sandwiched between WWII and Vietnam, it became 'the forgotten war' despite high casualties.
items.why: Conflict casualties are not just about combatant deaths. Korea's civilian toll, the bombing intensity and the legacy of an unresolved war shape East Asia today — but rarely feature in Cold War textbooks.

items.title: Cromwell did not set out to be a republican
items.claim: What were Oliver Cromwell's politics in 1642?

options.text: He had been a republican agitator since the 1620s
He was a Huntingdonshire MP and country gentleman who fought for Parliament against the king's policies but moved towards regicide only by late 1648
He was a paid Dutch agent from the start
He was a Leveller from the outset

items.reveal:
Cromwell entered the 1640 Long Parliament as MP for Cambridge. As late as 1647 he was negotiating with Charles I (the Heads of the Proposals). The king's plotting with the Scots — the Second Civil War of 1648 — convinced Cromwell that Charles could not be trusted.

Pride's Purge (December 1648) removed MPs likely to negotiate. The Rump Parliament tried and executed the king on 30 January 1649. Cromwell signed the death warrant but had not been pushing for it years earlier.

He later dissolved the Rump (1653) and accepted the title Lord Protector, refusing the crown in 1657.
items.why: The 'inevitable republican' Cromwell of memory is partly constructed by 19th-century liberals (Macaulay, Carlyle). The actual man's politics shifted under pressure of events.

items.title: Newton published the Principia in 1687

options.text: 'Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica' set out three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, deriving Kepler's planetary laws mathematically — uniting terrestrial and celestial physics
A defence of the Aristotelian universe
A treatise on biblical chronology only

items.reveal_title: Standing on the shoulders of giants
items.reveal:
The Principia was published in Latin in July 1687, funded by Edmond Halley after the Royal Society's stock of unsold fish books left it short of cash. Newton derived the inverse-square law of gravity, the three laws of motion, and applied them to planets, comets, the tides and the shape of the Earth.

Newton had developed calculus (his 'fluxions') in 1665-66 during the plague closure of Cambridge. He published Opticks in 1704 in English.

Newton became Master of the Mint in 1699, prosecuting counterfeiters. He served as President of the Royal Society from 1703 to 1727. His tomb is in Westminster Abbey.
items.why: Modern physics begins with one book. The unification of celestial and terrestrial mechanics in 1687 is the high-water mark of the Scientific Revolution — and remained the framework of physics until Einstein.
